# nish/net/url

The request target's path and query, split and percent-decoded in place, and its query string read as key/value pairs; and whole URLs, parsed into their parts and references resolved against them.

```ts
import {
  URL_DECODE_ALLOW_NUL,
  URL_DECODE_ERR_ESCAPE,
  URL_DECODE_ERR_NUL,
  URL_DECODE_ERR_SPACE,
  URL_DECODE_FORM,
  URL_DECODE_LENIENT,
  URL_DEFAULT_MAX_PAIRS,
  URL_QUERY_END,
  URL_QUERY_ERR_PAIRS,
  URL_QUERY_PAIR,
  Url,
  UrlPathSegments,
  UrlQuery,
  UrlQueryLimits,
  percentDecode,
  percentDecodeErrorAt,
  percentDecodePathSegment,
  urlDecode,
  urlDefaultPort,
  urlIsHostPort,
  urlOrigin,
  urlParse,
  urlQueryFind,
  urlQueryGet,
  urlQueryStart,
  urlResolve,
  urlSerialize,
} from "nish/net/url";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { UrlQuery, UrlQueryLimits, URL_DECODE_FORM, URL_QUERY_PAIR, percentDecode, urlQueryFind, urlQueryStart } from "nish/net/url";

const q: i32 = urlQueryStart(target, 0, len)    // -1: no `?`, so no query
if (q >= 0) {
  const query: UrlQuery = new UrlQuery(new UrlQueryLimits())
  query.reset(target, q + 1, len - q - 1)
  if (urlQueryFind(query, "name") === URL_QUERY_PAIR) {
    const n: i32 = percentDecode(target, query.valueStart, query.valueLength, out, 0, URL_DECODE_FORM)
    if (n >= 0) {
      // out[0, n) is the value
    } // else n is a URL_DECODE_ERR_* code: a peer's `%zz`, never read out
  }   // else no such key, or URL_QUERY_ERR_PAIRS past the cap
}
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-callout type="info">

A handler that routes on a path or reads `?name=…` from a query otherwise
writes its own byte scan, and each such scan decides differently what `%zz`,
`%00`, `+` or a hundred thousand `&` mean. This module decides once:

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="The byte API allocates nothing">

`urlQueryStart`, `percentDecode`,
`UrlPathSegments` and `UrlQuery` read a window `bytes[off, off + len)` and
answer offsets into it, or write into the caller's array; `reset` reuses an
iterator, so a server that holds one per connection allocates nothing per
request. No byte outside the window is read. A window outside its array, or
an `at` outside `out`, is a bug in the caller and panics; nothing a peer
sends does.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Decoding is strict unless asked otherwise">

With no flags,
`percentDecode` refuses a `%` not followed by two hex digits
(`URL_DECODE_ERR_ESCAPE`) and `%00` (`URL_DECODE_ERR_NUL`), and copies `+`
as it stands. `URL_DECODE_FORM` reads `+` as a space, as
`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` does; `URL_DECODE_LENIENT` copies a
malformed escape as it stands, as the WHATWG URL Standard's percent-decode
and `URLSearchParams` do; `URL_DECODE_ALLOW_NUL` decodes `%00` to a 0 byte.
For valid UTF-8, `URLSearchParams` is `URL_DECODE_FORM | URL_DECODE_LENIENT |
URL_DECODE_ALLOW_NUL`; it replaces an invalid sequence with U+FFFD.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Decoded bytes are bytes">

The byte API does not check that what it
decodes is UTF-8, where `decodeURIComponent` throws on `%FF`: a path segment
or a value may be binary, and whatever reads it as text checks it.
`urlDecode` and `urlQueryGet`, which answer a string, refuse anything that is
not valid UTF-8.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="A path is split before it is decoded">

`UrlPathSegments` splits on the
raw `/` only, and `percentDecodePathSegment` decodes one segment, so `%2F`
is a 0x2F byte inside its segment and never starts a new one: `/a%2Fb/c` is
the two segments `a/b` and `c`. `+` is literal in a path.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="A query yields at most `UrlQueryLimits.maxPairs` pairs">

**A query yields at most `UrlQueryLimits.maxPairs` pairs** (100 by default),
and past it `next()` answers `URL_QUERY_ERR_PAIRS` and stays spent. Empty
pairs (`a&&b`, a leading or trailing `&`) are skipped and not counted, as
`URLSearchParams` skips them.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="A fragment is not part of a request target">

**A fragment is not part of a request target** (RFC 9112 §3.2), so the byte
API never looks for a `#`: in a target that holds one, it is a byte of the
path or of the last value.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="A whole URL is parsed strictly, and nothing in it is decoded">

A client
that is handed `http://…` by a user, a redirect or a link needs its host and
port before it connects, and the place each reference points to:

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { Url, urlOrigin, urlParse, urlResolve, urlSerialize } from "nish/net/url";

const base: Url | null = urlParse("https://example.com/a/b?q")
if (base !== null) {
  const next: Url | null = urlResolve(base, "../c#top")  // https://example.com/c#top
  // next.host, next.port (-1: the default), urlOrigin(next) === "https://example.com:443"
}
```

</scalar-code-group>

</scalar-detail>

`urlParse` and `urlResolve` follow RFC 3986 (§3 for the parts, §5.2 to
resolve, dot segments removed) and refuse, with null, what two readers could
take for different hosts: a byte outside printable ASCII, a backslash, a
malformed `%`, a second `@`, a percent-encoded or otherwise non-unreserved
host byte, a host that looks numeric but is not a strict dotted-decimal IPv4
address (`127.1`, `0x7f.0.0.1`, `2130706433`), an IPv6 zone or IPvFuture
literal, and a port past 65535. The scheme and host are lower-cased; every
other part is kept as written, still percent-encoded.

The record of what this module refuses and why is `docs/security/url.md`.

## Functions

### percentDecode

Percent-decodes `src[off, off + len)` into `out` from `out[at]` on, and
answers the number of bytes written, or a negative `URL_DECODE_ERR_*` code;
`flags` is a sum of `URL_DECODE_*` (0 is strict: malformed escapes and `%00`
refused, `+` kept). Decoding never makes the input longer, so `len` bytes
of room always suffice; with less, `URL_DECODE_ERR_SPACE` is answered before
any write at or past `out.length`. On an error the bytes before it have been
written. What is decoded is not checked as UTF-8.

```ts
function percentDecode(
  src: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  flags: i32,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="src" type="u8[]" required>

The array holding the encoded text.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the encoded text starts in `src`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

The encoded text's length in bytes; a window outside `src` panics.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array the decoded bytes are written into.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The index in `out` the first decoded byte goes to; one below 0 or above `out.length` panics.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="flags" type="i32" required>

`URL_DECODE_FORM`, `URL_DECODE_LENIENT` and `URL_DECODE_ALLOW_NUL`, summed, or 0 for strict.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

How many bytes were written from `out[at]` on, or `URL_DECODE_ERR_ESCAPE`, `URL_DECODE_ERR_NUL` or `URL_DECODE_ERR_SPACE`.

</scalar-field>

### percentDecodeErrorAt

The offset in `src` of the byte `percentDecode` with the same arguments
fails at — the `%` of a malformed escape or of `%00`, or the first byte
`out` has no room for — or -1 when it does not fail. It writes what
`percentDecode` would have written before the error.

```ts
function percentDecodeErrorAt(
  src: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  flags: i32,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="src" type="u8[]" required>

The array holding the encoded text.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the encoded text starts in `src`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

The encoded text's length in bytes; a window outside `src` panics.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array the decoded bytes are written into, as `percentDecode` writes them.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The index in `out` the first decoded byte goes to; one below 0 or above `out.length` panics.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="flags" type="i32" required>

The `URL_DECODE_*` sum `percentDecode` was given.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The index in `src` decoding stops at, or -1 when all of it decodes.

</scalar-field>

### percentDecodePathSegment

`percentDecode` for one path segment: `+` is literal whatever `flags` say,
and `%2F` is a 0x2F byte in the segment. Split the path with
`UrlPathSegments` first, then decode each segment.

```ts
function percentDecodePathSegment(
  src: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  flags: i32,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="src" type="u8[]" required>

The array holding the path.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the segment starts in `src`, as `UrlPathSegments` gives it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

The segment's length in bytes; a window outside `src` panics.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array the decoded bytes are written into.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The index in `out` the first decoded byte goes to; one below 0 or above `out.length` panics.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="flags" type="i32" required>

A `URL_DECODE_*` sum; `URL_DECODE_FORM` in it is ignored.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

How many bytes were written from `out[at]` on, or a negative `URL_DECODE_ERR_*` code, as `percentDecode` answers.

</scalar-field>

### urlDecode

`s` percent-decoded with `flags`, or null when `percentDecode` refuses it
or what it decodes to is not valid UTF-8, which is where
`decodeURIComponent` throws. `s` is expected to be ASCII, as a URL on the
wire is. It allocates its answer.

```ts
function urlDecode(
  s: string,
  flags: i32,
): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

The encoded text; a code unit past 0xFF (possible only under Node) answers null.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="flags" type="i32" required>

`URL_DECODE_FORM`, `URL_DECODE_LENIENT` and `URL_DECODE_ALLOW_NUL`, summed, or 0 for strict.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string | null">

The decoded text, or null for a refused escape or `%00`, or text that is not UTF-8.

</scalar-field>

### urlDefaultPort

The port a scheme uses when a URL names none.

```ts
function urlDefaultPort(scheme: string): i32
```

<scalar-field name="scheme" type="string" required>

The scheme, lower-cased and without its `:`, as `Url.scheme` holds it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

80 for `http` and `ws`, 443 for `https` and `wss`, and -1 for any other scheme.

</scalar-field>

### urlIsHostPort

Whether `bytes[a, b)` is `uri-host [ ":" port ]` (RFC 3986 §3.2.2, §3.2.3)
by the rules `urlParse` holds a URL's host and port to: a bracketed IPv6
address, a dotted-decimal IPv4 address, or a reg-name of unreserved bytes
that does not read as a number, then an optional `:` and a port of digits
up to 65535. An empty host and an empty port are allowed, as in a URL; a
percent-encoded or sub-delims byte in a reg-name is not. It is the rule an
HTTP server holds a `Host` field to (RFC 9112 §3.2). Allocates nothing.

```ts
function urlIsHostPort(
  bytes: u8[],
  a: i32,
  b: i32,
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="bytes" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes that hold the value.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="a" type="i32" required>

The index of the value's first byte.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="b" type="i32" required>

The index past the value's last byte.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the bytes are a host and an optional port; false otherwise, and for a window outside `bytes`.

</scalar-field>

### urlOrigin

`u`'s origin as `scheme://host:port`, the port always written (the scheme's
default when `u` names none), so origins compare as plain strings:
`http://A.com/x` and `http://a.com:80/y` are both `http://a.com:80`. Null for
a scheme other than http, https, ws or wss, which has no origin to compare.
Hosts are compared as written, lower-cased, so `[::1]` and `[0::1]` are
different origins, and so are `a.com.` and `a.com`: equal strings are the
same origin, and a split errs toward "different".

```ts
function urlOrigin(u: Url): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="u" type="Url" required>

The URL whose origin is wanted.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string | null">

The origin, such as `https://example.com:443`, or null for a scheme with no default port.

</scalar-field>

### urlParse

The absolute URL `s` split into its parts, or null when it is not one this
module accepts.

`s` is refused when it has no scheme, holds a byte outside printable ASCII (a
control byte, a space, DEL or anything past 0x7F), a backslash or a `%` not
followed by two hex digits, or its authority has more than one `@`, a host
with a byte outside RFC 3986's unreserved set (so a percent-encoded one), a
host whose last label is numeric but that is not a dotted-decimal IPv4
address, a malformed IPv6 literal or a port that is not digits or is
above 65535. An http, https, ws or wss URL needs a non-empty host.

The path's dot segments are removed, as RFC 3986 §5.2.2 removes them from a
reference with a scheme. Nothing is decoded. It allocates its answer.

```ts
function urlParse(s: string): Url | null
```

<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

The absolute URL, such as `https://example.com/a?b#c`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Url | null">

The URL's parts, still percent-encoded, `scheme` and `host` lower-cased; or null when `s` is refused.

</scalar-field>

### urlQueryFind

Moves `q` on to the first of its remaining pairs whose key, decoded in form
mode, equals `name`, and answers `URL_QUERY_PAIR` with `q`'s windows on it;
or `URL_QUERY_END`, or the error `next()` answered. Nothing is allocated.
`?na%6De=x` holds the key `name`; a key with a malformed escape or `%00`
matches nothing. Call it again for the next pair with the same key.
`name` is ASCII: natively it is compared with the key's bytes, under Node
with its UTF-16 code units, so a non-ASCII name answers differently.

```ts
function urlQueryFind(
  q: UrlQuery,
  name: string,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="q" type="UrlQuery" required>

The query iterator, moved on past the pair found; its windows bound that pair.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="name" type="string" required>

The key to look for, as it reads decoded.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

`URL_QUERY_PAIR` when a pair with the key was found, `URL_QUERY_END` when none is left, or the negative `URL_QUERY_ERR_*` code `next()` answered.

</scalar-field>

### urlQueryGet

The first value for `name` in the query of the request target `target`,
form-decoded strictly: `""` for a key written without `=`, as
`URLSearchParams.get` answers, and null when the target has no query, the
key is absent, the value is malformed or not UTF-8, or the key comes after
`URL_DEFAULT_MAX_PAIRS` pairs. It allocates its answer.

```ts
function urlQueryGet(
  target: string,
  name: string,
): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="target" type="string" required>

A request target such as `/search?q=nish`; everything after its first `?` is the query.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="name" type="string" required>

The key to look for, as it reads decoded; ASCII, as `urlQueryFind` asks.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string | null">

The first decoded value for `name`, `""` when it has no `=`, or null in the cases above.

</scalar-field>

### urlQueryStart

The index of the first `?` in `bytes[off, off + len)`, or -1 when there is
none. The path is `[off, q)` and the query `(q, off + len)`; nothing is
copied. A `#` is not looked for: a request target holds no fragment.

```ts
function urlQueryStart(
  bytes: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="bytes" type="u8[]" required>

The array holding the request target.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the target starts in `bytes`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

The target's length in bytes; a window outside `bytes` panics.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The index in `bytes` of the `?`, or -1 when the target has no query.

</scalar-field>

### urlResolve

The reference `ref` resolved against the absolute URL `base` by RFC 3986
§5.2.2, strictly (`http:g` is `http:g`, not relative), or null when `ref`
breaks a rule `urlParse` names or what it resolves to is an http, https, ws
or wss URL without a host. `base`'s fragment is never carried over. It
allocates its answer and does not change `base`.

```ts
function urlResolve(
  base: Url,
  ref: string,
): Url | null
```

<scalar-field name="base" type="Url" required>

The URL `ref` is relative to, as `urlParse` made it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ref" type="string" required>

The reference: an absolute URL, a network-path `//host/p`, an absolute path, a relative path, a query or a fragment.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Url | null">

The resolved URL, still percent-encoded, or null when `ref` is refused or resolves to a URL without a host its scheme needs.

</scalar-field>

### urlSerialize

`u` written back as RFC 3986 §5.3 recomposes it, an IPv6 host in brackets.
The userinfo is written when either half is non-empty. A path that starts
with `//` under no authority is written after `/.`, as the WHATWG URL
Standard writes it, so the string does not read back with an authority.

```ts
function urlSerialize(u: Url): string
```

<scalar-field name="u" type="Url" required>

The URL to write; its parts are written as they are held, so still percent-encoded.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

The URL as one string, scheme to fragment.

</scalar-field>

## Classes

### Url

A URL split into its parts (RFC 3986 §3). Each part is held as it was
written, still percent-encoded, except that `scheme` and `host` are
lower-cased. `urlParse` and `urlResolve` make one; `urlSerialize` writes one
back.

```ts
class Url
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Url()` |  |
| `fragment: string \| null` | Without its `#`, or null when there is no `#`. |
| `hasAuthority: boolean` | True when the URL has a `//` authority; `mailto:a@b` has none and `file:///x` has an empty one. |
| `host: string` | A lower-cased reg-name, a dotted IPv4 address, or an IPv6 address without its brackets. |
| `password: string` | The userinfo after its first `:`, as written; empty when there is none. |
| `path: string` | With its dot segments removed; empty, or starting with `/` when there is an authority. |
| `port: i32` | 0 to 65535, or -1 when the URL names none; `urlOrigin` supplies the scheme's default. |
| `query: string \| null` | Without its `?`, or null when there is no `?`. |
| `scheme: string` | Lower-cased, without its `:`: `http`. |
| `username: string` | The userinfo before its first `:`, as written; empty when there is none. |

### UrlPathSegments

The segments of a path, split on the raw `/`. A leading `/` starts the
path rather than an empty segment, so `/a//b/` is `a`, ``, `b`, ``, `/` is
one empty segment and an empty window has none. Each segment's raw bytes
are `bytes[start, start + length)`; decode one with
`percentDecodePathSegment`.

```ts
class UrlPathSegments
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new UrlPathSegments()` | An iterator over nothing until `reset`. |
| `bytes: u8[]` | The array the path is read from, as `reset` was given it. |
| `length: i32` | The current segment's length in raw bytes. |
| `start: i32` | The current segment's first byte. |
| `next(): boolean` | Moves to the next segment, whose bytes `start` and `length` then name. |
| `reset(bytes: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): void` | Starts over on the path `bytes[off, off + len)`; panics when the window is outside the array. |

### UrlQuery

The pairs of a query string, one per `next()`, in order. The window is the
query without its `?`. `&` separates pairs and the first `=` in a pair ends
its key: `a&b=&c=d=e` is `a` with no value, `b` with an empty one and `c`
with `d=e`. A key's raw bytes are `bytes[keyStart, keyStart + keyLength)`
and a value's `bytes[valueStart, valueStart + valueLength)`; decode them
with `percentDecode` and `URL_DECODE_FORM`.

```ts
class UrlQuery
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new UrlQuery(limits: UrlQueryLimits)` | An iterator over nothing until `reset`, with the cap in `limits`. |
| `failed: i32` | 0, or the `URL_QUERY_ERR_*` code every later `next()` answers. |
| `hasValue: boolean` | False for a pair written without `=` (`a`), true for `a=` with `valueLength` 0. |
| `keyLength: i32` | The current pair's key length in raw bytes. |
| `keyStart: i32` | Where the current pair's key starts in `bytes`. |
| `valueLength: i32` | The current pair's value length in raw bytes, 0 when it has none. |
| `valueStart: i32` | Where the current pair's value starts in `bytes`. |
| `next(): i32` | Moves to the next pair, setting the key and value windows. |
| `reset(bytes: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): void` | Starts over on the query `bytes[off, off + len)`, clearing `failed`; panics when the window is outside the array. |

### UrlQueryLimits

What a `UrlQuery` refuses to yield. The iterator copies the number when it
is made; a negative cap is read as zero, so every query with a pair fails.

```ts
class UrlQueryLimits
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new UrlQueryLimits()` |  |
| `maxPairs: i32` | The most pairs one query yields, `URL_DEFAULT_MAX_PAIRS` (a field starts at a literal); past it `next()` answers `URL_QUERY_ERR_PAIRS` and stays spent. |

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`URL_DECODE_ALLOW_NUL: i32`

`%00` decodes to a 0 byte rather than being refused.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`URL_DECODE_ERR_ESCAPE: i32`

A `%` not followed by two hex digits: `%zz`, or `%4` or `%` at the end of the window.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`URL_DECODE_ERR_NUL: i32`

`%00` without `URL_DECODE_ALLOW_NUL`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`URL_DECODE_ERR_SPACE: i32`

`out` has no room for the next byte; nothing is written at or past `out.length`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`URL_DECODE_FORM: i32`

`+` is a space, as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` writes one.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`URL_DECODE_LENIENT: i32`

A `%` not followed by two hex digits is copied as it stands rather than refused (WHATWG percent-decode).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="100" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`URL_DEFAULT_MAX_PAIRS: i32`

The default for `UrlQueryLimits.maxPairs`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`URL_QUERY_END: i32`

The window holds no more pairs; every later `next()` answers the same.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`URL_QUERY_ERR_PAIRS: i32`

The query holds more than `maxPairs` pairs; sticky in `failed`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`URL_QUERY_PAIR: i32`

`next()` found a pair; the iterator's windows bound it.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
